criteria.description: Correctly applies Sylvester's criterion to G1, concluding PD.
Correctly applies Sylvester's criterion to G2, concluding NOT PD.
Explains or demonstrates concretely what goes wrong for G2 (e.g. exhibits a v with v^T G2 v < 0).

commonErrors: Only checking the diagonal entries are positive without checking the determinant condition (a common shortcut that misses non-PD matrices with positive diagonals, like G2 here).

solutions.fullSolution:
G1: a=2>0, ad-b^2=2*2-1^2=3>0. Both Sylvester conditions hold, so G1 is PD, a valid metric tensor.
G2: a=1>0, but ad-b^2=1*1-2^2=1-4=-3<0. Fails the second condition, so G2 is NOT PD. Concretely, for v=(1,-1): v^T G2 v = 1*1*1 + 1*2*(-1) + (-1)*2*1 + (-1)*1*(-1) = 1-2-2+1 = -2 < 0, directly violating the positive-definiteness requirement.

criteria.description: Correctly rewrites <e_i,x> = e_i^T x as a scalar and reassembles P(x) = (sum_i e_i e_i^T) x.
Correctly identifies sum_i e_i e_i^T = UU^T.
Correctly computes U^T U = I_k using orthonormality.
Correctly concludes P^2 = U I_k U^T = UU^T = P.

commonErrors: Confusing U^T U (a k x k matrix, = I_k) with U U^T (an n x n matrix, = P, generally NOT the identity unless k=n).

solutions.fullSolution:
(a) <e_i,x> = e_i^T x (standard dot product), a scalar, so e_i<e_i,x> = e_i(e_i^T x) = (e_i e_i^T) x (outer product times x). Summing: P(x) = sum_i (e_i e_i^T) x = (sum_i e_i e_i^T) x. Since U=[e_1 .. e_k] has the e_i as columns, sum_i e_i e_i^T is exactly the matrix product U U^T. So P = UU^T.
(b) P^2 = (UU^T)(UU^T) = U(U^T U)U^T. The (i,j) entry of U^T U is e_i^T e_j = <e_i,e_j> = delta_ij (orthonormality), so U^T U = I_k. Therefore P^2 = U I_k U^T = UU^T = P, confirming idempotency: P is a genuine projection.
